resumen: A telephoto lens, a fast shutter speed and patience to photograph animals without disturbing them.

bloques.alt: A bird perched on a branch, seen from the side. On the left, a camera at the same height as the bird's eye, with a dotted line between them. A focus square marks the eye: 1, eye in focus. The camera is at the animal's level: 2, at its level. Behind, the background is blurry and clean: 3, clean background.
bloques.pie: 1 Focus on the eye. 2 Get to the animal's level. 3 A clean, blurry background.

bloques.texto: With animals, you don't get closer: your lens does. Fast shutter speed, the eye in focus and patience.

A frightened animal leaves or changes its behavior, and getting too close can disturb it, especially if there is a nest. Use a telephoto lens or a long zoom (more in “Focal lengths”), move slowly and without sudden gestures, and if the animal gets restless, back off. Stay still and wait for it to calm down.

items: A fast [[velocidad|shutter speed]]: 1/1000 s or faster if the animal flies or runs. It's the same principle as in “Sports photography”.
A wide-open [[apertura|aperture]]: more light gets in for that short shutter speed and the background comes out blurrier.
[[enfoque-continuo|Continuous focus]] and [[rafaga|burst]]: the camera follows the animal and then you pick the best photo.
Focus on the eye: if it's sharp, the photo works.

bloques.texto: Many animals are more active at sunrise and sunset, in the soft, warm light of the [[hora-dorada|golden hour]]. Get to the level of their eyes, even if you have to crouch or lie down: the photo feels closer than if you shoot from above. And look at the background: a clean one makes the animal stand out.

On many phones the zoom doesn't reach nearly as far as a telephoto lens: don't get closer to the animal, wait for it to come closer. Tap the screen on the animal to focus, as in “Tap to focus and expose”, and take a burst.
Find a place with birds, like the edge of a pond or a tree with birds, and sit still for a while. When they move, take a burst with a fast shutter speed and count how many come out sharp.
